messages:
Anjali (eng-sec): quick sync — i'm opening this thread to capture the longhaul authn refactor concerns for operator flows. wanted to list the tradeoffs and get alignment on migration strategy.
Kevin (platform): +1. do we have a short problem statement?
Anjali (eng-sec): problem: operator processes (deploys, autoscaler, admin tooling) currently use long-lived API keys that overlap project namespaces. this complicates RBAC, auditing, and key rotation. we need a path that: minimizes customer disruption, preserves operator performance, and makes least-privilege enforceable.
Marta (serving): is this mainly about machine-to-service keys vs human API keys?
Anjali (eng-sec): yes. also about operator identity (operator service) vs per-project operator tokens. two axes: identity granularity and token lifetime/attestation.
Liam (sre): our ops runbooks rely on the existing keys for cross-project workflows. any migration needs a fallback path.
Kevin (platform): sketch of options: 1) namespace-prefix API keys (operator:project-<id>-<rand>), 2) ephemeral operator tokens minted per-run, 3) operator proxy service that translates operator key -> per-project scoped auth.
Marta (serving): option 1 is low friction but doesn't solve least-privilege (still long-lived). option 2 better for security but adds latency and token broker work.
Anjali (eng-sec): agreed. option 3 centralizes translation and lets us audit translation events, but becomes a critical-path service and needs high availability.
Kevin (platform): list of tradeoffs i'm thinking:
- Security: ephemeral tokens > brokered-per-run > long-lived namespaced keys
- Complexity: namespaced keys (low) < proxy (medium) < ephemeral broker (high)
- Rollout friction: namespaced keys easiest to roll out with client shims
- Observability: proxy gives best single-pane audit events
Marta (serving): also cost: ephemeral brokers increase token ops (QPS), might need sharding and caching for scale. same for proxy.
Liam (sre): fallback plan must support a quick switch to legacy keys in case of partial failures. propose: feature flag + canary route that sends X% to new path.
Anjali (eng-sec): proposal: two-stage migration: A) introduce namespaced operator keys (per-project prefix) immediately; B) build operator-bridge proxy as a short-lived _shim_ that handles token translation, with metrics and circuit breakers; C) iterate to ephemeral minting for high-security customers.
Kevin (platform): is there a compatibility shim we can ship in the console SDKs and infra agents so existing tasks pick up prefixes without human intervention?
Marta (serving): yes — mint at agent start if missing. simple: agent checks metadata for operator-id and requests namespaced key via /internal/keys endpoint. fallback to existing key if endpoint errors.
Anjali (eng-sec): we should be explicit about claims mapping: operator-bridge should emit claims: {"actor":"operator-service","project":"<proj>","flow":"deploy"}. keep the token short TTL (1h) and require signed attestation from KMS.
Liam (sre): don't forget rate limits: bridge will see spikes during rollouts. need autoscaling + per-caller quotas.
Kevin (platform): telemetry plan: track issuer->project mapping counts, bridge latency p50/p95, token failure rate, fallback to legacy rate. create an alert when fallback > 1% for 10m.
Marta (serving): rollout checklist suggestion:
- alpha: internal operator-only canary (10% internal jobs)
- beta: opt-in customers + opt-out flag for 2 weeks
- ga: default on, with migration window + deprecation notice for legacy keys
Anjali (eng-sec): migration data model: store map of operator-id -> allowed projects and scopes. this replaces the old free-form API key permissions. must be queryable by audit tooling.
Kevin (platform): question: how do we present RBAC to tenant admins? do we expose 'operator roles' in console or keep it hidden?
Anjali (eng-sec): recommendation: expose a minimal view: operator name, assigned projects, and scope level (read/write/admin). full mapping lives in sec catalog.
Liam (sre): ops consideration: we should add a pre-check CLI command that simulates issuance to detect missing bindings before we flip.
devx-bot: reminder — RFC follow-up meeting scheduled Thu 10:30. added agenda item: "operator-bridge availability SLOs".
Kevin (platform): open questions:
- token proof format: do we use JWTs signed by KMS or opaque tokens with backend introspection?
- per-project caching: do we let bridge cache project-policy lookups for 5m?
- migration TTL: how long do we keep legacy key support?
Marta (serving): jwt signed by KMS is easiest for downstream services (no introspection). but key rotation and jwks propagation needs handling. opaque + introspect centralizes rotation but adds latency.
Anjali (eng-sec): lean toward short-lived JWTs (signed, kid header) with introspection endpoint for revocation. that gives downstream low-latency verification and still allows rapid revocation.
Liam (sre): cache policy lookups with short TTL (30s-5m) and hard invalidate on policy-change events. don't rely on long caches.
Kevin (platform): propose legacy-support window: 90 days from GA, with a deprecation banner in console and telemetry to track active legacy keys.
Anjali (eng-sec): decision log draft:
- immediate: implement namespaced operator keys + SDK shim (low effort)
- next: operator-bridge proxy with authn attestation, p50 < 50ms target, circuit breaker + retry policy
- future: ephemeral minting for customers that require it (opt-in)
- tokens: short-lived signed JWTs + introspect endpoint for revocation
- migration window: 90 days post-GA
Marta (serving): i'll add resource estimates for the bridge (pods, memory, QPS).
Liam (sre): i'll draft runbook changes and alert thresholds.
Kevin (platform): i'll update the RFC with the decision log and open PR for SDK shim.
Anjali (eng-sec): thanks all. if no objections i'll lock this as the plan tomorrow and include the canary schedule in the RFC.
Kevin (platform): no objections from me.
Marta (serving): lgtm
Liam (sre): lgtm
Anjali (eng-sec): ok locking plan. follow-up: assign owners and add tickets for: shard/caching, circuit breakers, telemetry + console banner.
devx-bot: ticket created: #INF-4092 operator-bridge-prototype (owner: Marta).
